appraisal_events.evidence: « ne plaignez pas trop Saint-Loup... Je crois qu'il ne peut être nulle part mieux que là. »
appraisal_events.explanation: The duchess dismisses the princesse's worry and reframes Saint-Loup's risky posting as fine, even enviable, though her attention is largely on her own social connections rather than genuine concern for him.

status_effects.explanation: His situation is reframed positively by the duchess (chosen post, nothing to pity), a mild local elevation despite the surrounding worry about him.

ambiguities: The duchess's reassurance about Saint-Loup could reflect genuine positive regard or merely performative, self-focused chatter (she is more preoccupied with naming her own influential contacts); the local positive framing is scored conservatively given this uncertainty.
Elstir is mentioned only as the painter of a similar flower recalled by the narrator's memory; this is a purely referential mention with no local evaluative or social content, so he was not scored.

Le narrateur appears only as the perceiving/remembering consciousness (recognizing a flower Elstir had painted) and is not staged as a social participant in this passage, so he was not scored per the instructions.
